idiom_name: plain class over a dict with a list-of-operations journal
implementation_notes: Duck typing makes the fake an ordinary class: a dict holds the state, a list the journal, and the accessor is a normal method, so nothing of the classic structure has to be built and no framework is needed for the working half. unittest.mock records calls on mocks and spies - call_args_list, mock_calls, assert_called_with - but does not implement behaviour; Mock(wraps=fake) is the library way to add raw recording to a real implementation when domain-level journal entries are not required, which places it in the spy row. Prefer the hand-written journal when assertions should read as domain operations, keep a fresh fake per test (no module-level state), and consider typing.Protocol plus a shared contract test to keep the fake honest against the real collaborator.
pitfalls: A mutable default argument or a module-level journal is shared by every test - initialise store and journal per instance.
Storing references to mutable arguments records aliases, not history; copy the values the system under test may mutate.
unittest.mock's call_args_list records every raw call, including incidental ones; asserting it wholesale couples the test to the system under test's call pattern.
